api_analysis.hypothesis: The existing custom_ops.cu exports reduce_mean_dim1_launcher and mul_scalar_launcher with extern "C" signatures. A binding file must be created to expose these to Python under the names reduce_mean_dim1 and mul_scalar, with proper dtype/device/shape validation, stride-aware launcher invocation, and REGISTER_BINDING registration.
evidence: SKILL.md requires binding files in kernels/*_binding.cpp and prohibits torch operators in .cpp; only tensor creation/allocation via torch::empty_like is allowed.
custom_ops.cu defines extern "C" launchers reduce_mean_dim1_launcher and mul_scalar_launcher taking raw float pointers, strides, dimensions, and cudaStream_t.
model_new.py calls cuda_extension.reduce_mean_dim1(x) and cuda_extension.mul_scalar(x, float(self.out_channels)).

task_contract.json and custom_ops_contract.json specify reduce_mean_dim1 expects 4D tensor, returns [N,1,H,W]; mul_scalar takes tensor and float scalar, returns same shape; both support strides and are float32 CUDA.
changes: Create kernels/custom_ops_binding.cpp with includes torch/types.h, torch/csrc/utils/pybind.h, cuda_runtime.h, c10/cuda/CUDAStream.h, ../binding_registry.h.
Declare extern "C" launchers matching custom_ops.cu signatures.

Implement reduce_mean_dim1 wrapper: validate 4D CPU? Actually CUDA only, float32, device; check dims; allocate output via torch::empty with shape [N,1,H,W] same options as input; get current stream; call launcher with raw pointers and strides; return output.
Implement mul_scalar wrapper: validate float32 CUDA 4D; allocate output like input; call launcher with scalar converted to float; return output.
Use REGISTER_BINDING(custom_ops, register_custom_ops) with function registering both ops.
Ensure no torch ops used for computation; only torch::empty for allocation and tensor properties.
Remove any potential accidental duplicate registration.
